name: Platysmaplasty (neck band surgery)

image.caption: Closure of access incision after platysmaplasty in neck lift surgery

lead: Platysmaplasty tightens or reshapes the platysma, the thin muscle sheet across the front of the neck, to remove visible vertical bands and give a smoother, sharper neck contour. It is usually done as part of a neck lift or facelift, sometimes together with removal of fat under the chin.

Surgeons plicate, cut or suture the platysma, for example in the corset pattern described in 1990 for persistent bands and contour irregularities, so the muscle sits flatter beneath the skin. The published literature is mainly surgeons' technique papers and case series.

paras: It is performed by a surgeon under anesthesia, typically alongside a neck lift or facelift. The contour change shows once swelling settles after healing. In looksmaxxing communities it is grouped with hardmaxxing procedures for a sharper jawline and neck.

Hematoma is the most common complication of related facelift surgery. Persistent bands and contour irregularities have been reported with some techniques. As with any operation under anesthesia, surgical and anesthetic risks apply.

angle.text: Platysmaplasty removes visible vertical neck bands and sharpens the neck contour by tightening the platysma muscle, usually alongside a neck lift or facelift. The change in contour is visible once healing is complete. The literature consists of surgeons' technique papers and case series.

lead: Platysmaplasty is a surgical procedure that modifies the platysma, the thin sheet of muscle across the front of the neck, to reduce visible vertical neck bands and improve the neck contour. It is usually performed as part of a neck lift or facelift, sometimes together with removal of submental fat [1][2][3].

Published literature consists mainly of surgeons' technique descriptions and case series. Techniques include midline plication, muscle resection or transection, and the corset platysmaplasty, which was described in 1990 to address persistent bands and contour irregularities seen after earlier methods [1]. Hematoma is described as the most common complication of related facelift surgery [4]. In looksmaxxing communities it is grouped with hardmaxxing procedures aimed at a sharper jawline and neck.

paras: Surgeons modify the platysma by tightening it at the midline, resecting or cutting it, or suturing it in a corset-like pattern [1]. Limited-incision approaches combining submental lipectomy with platysmaplasty have also been published [3]. Anatomical work has analysed platysma suspension during neck lift in a series of 30 cases [5]. A surgeon's 2014 update describes a neck lift strategy aiming to control the size, shape and position of each neck feature, drawing on 522 consecutive procedures [2].

A review of 1078 consecutive facelifts examined factors associated with hematoma, described as the most common complication of rhytidectomy and a cause of prolonged swelling or skin necrosis [4]. A preliminary report described local infiltration of tranexamic acid to reduce intraoperative bleeding during facelifts [6]. Persistent or recurrent bands, visible submandibular gland bulges and contour irregularities were the shortcomings that prompted the corset technique [1].

Thread-lift sutures and barbed sutures have been reviewed as less invasive options in aesthetic surgery [7][8]. A paired report of identical twins undergoing facelifts with different techniques gave 10-year follow-up comparison [9].

Evidence is largely retrospective case series and technique papers rather than randomized trials. Reported examples include a 1078-facelift hematoma review [4], 522 neck lifts reviewed by one surgeon [2], a 30-case anatomical analysis [5], and a 10-year twin comparison [9]. A systematic review of thread-lift sutures concerns a related, less invasive approach [7].

timeline.event: Corset platysmaplasty described in Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery [1].
Limited-incision submental lipectomy with platysmaplasty reported [3].
A surgeon publishes an update on his neck-lift approach based on 522 cases [2].
